## Part A
```{r}
## Question 1
worker_age <- c(34, 28, 22, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29,
                35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49,
                50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 37, 43, 53, 41, 51,
                35, 24, 33, 41, 53, 40, 18, 44, 38, 41,
                48, 27, 39, 19, 30, 61, 54, 58, 26, 18)
print(worker_age)
```
## b. how many data points?
## Answer: There are 50 data points
```{r}
## c.  Find the minimum and the maximum value of worker’s age.
min(worker_age)
max(worker_age)
```
```{r}
## d. Access the 13rd to 18th elements and 33th to 35th elements of worker’s Age.
worker_age[13:18]
worker_age[33:35]
```
```{r}
## e. Access all but the 10th, 20th, 30th and 40th elements are not included.
worker_age[-c(10, 20, 30, 40)]
```
```{r}
## f. Modify the 4th, 14th, 24th, and 44th elements with value = 0.
worker_age[c(4, 14, 24, 44)] <- 0
print(worker_age)
```
```{r}
## Question 2: 
## a. Get the number of elements (length) in rivers, their sum (sum), mean (mean), median(median), variance(var), standard deviation(sd), minimum (min) and maximum (max).
length(rivers)  # Number of elements
sum(rivers)     # Sum
mean(rivers)    # Mean
median(rivers)  # Median
var(rivers)     # Variance
sd(rivers)      # Standard deviation
min(rivers)     # Minimum
max(rivers)     # Maximum
```
```{r}
## b. What is the result? The derived result must be in just one(1) vector name.
river_stats <- c(
  length(rivers),
  sum(rivers),
  mean(rivers),
  median(rivers),
  var(rivers),
  sd(rivers),
  min(rivers),
  max(rivers)
)

print(river_stats)
```

## Question #3

)

  67, 90, 225, 110, 90, 332, 302, 41, 52, 88,

```{r}
## Question 4. reate a list of ten (10) vegetables you ate during your lifetime. If none, just list down the vegetables in your mind.
vegetables <- list(
  "Carrot",
  "Potato",
  "Cabbage",
  "Broccoli",
  "Spinach",
  "Eggplant",
  "Squash",
  "Cauliflower",
  "Okra",
  "Lettuce"
)
## a. Add 2 additional vegetables after the last vegetables in the list. What is the result?
vegetables <- list(
  "Carrot", "Potato", "Cabbage", "Broccoli",
  "Spinach", "Eggplant", "Squash", "Cauliflower",
  "Okra", "Lettuce"
)

vegetables <- append(vegetables, list("Bell Pepper", "Radish"))

print(vegetables)
length(vegetables)
```
```{r}
## b. How many data points do you have?
## Answer: 
length(vegetables)
```
```{r}
## c. Add 4 additional vegetables after index 5. What is the result?
vegetables <- append(vegetables,
                     list("Onion", "Garlic", "Tomato", "Cucumber"),
                     after = 5)

print(vegetables)
```
```{r}
## d. How many datapoints does your vegetable list have?
length(vegetables)
```
